We found out the game was takign a LOT of memory for how simple the game is due to how unity handles game objects.

We've moved a lot of assets to the new Addressables system so that we can serve them from our CDN instead. Huge performance boost. notes.title: Raid Area 51 Game - December: Last Month of Updates
notes.content:
[h1]Raid Area 51 Game[/h1]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1142130/They_Cant_Stop_All_Of_Us/]Storm Area 51 Game[/url] Allows you to raid area 51 with friends.

[h1]Please Read First[/h1]
[b]Message from current Developers: The game is LIVE and we are continuing development on it.  We took over the game from Blake in February of 2020 and continue to improve and optimize the game for everyone. We thank Blake for creating this game and allowing us to continue the work on it.[/b]


[h2]The Raid Area 51 Game Story[/h2]
This game started off as a meme idea between me and my friend and has since then become so much more than that.

My name is Blake Gillman, I'm 19 years old and all I've wanted to do my entire life is game development. I'm autistic & lack any sort of a social life as I've dedicated almost my entire life now to games. Every day after school through both Middle School & High School I did game development, learning programming, learning how to model, to make textures, the basics of UI concept design, networking, marketing, etc.

The first time I released a game on Steam was in 2018 (Deep Space), just a little over a year ago. It was met with overwhelming negativity and I thought I wasn't cut out to be a game developer, I thought that my career was over, and I became suicidal and about a week later quit my job.

But as I said, I've been doing game development every day for years and I knew I could do better. By early of this year I had started my new job of picking up game development programming contracts which usually lasted a month or two in order to get by. I kept getting told that I was the fastest & most efficient programmer they'd ever worked with, but this didn't help my confidence, after all my last big game was such a failure. But then They Can't Stop All Of Us happened.

It started off as a joke I suggested to my friend. I browse & participate in Reddit often on the r/dankemes subreddit and at the time the "Raid area 51" meme was very popular. I thought it might be a cool idea to make a game about it, just a small game that would only take about a month to make about raiding area 51. Maybe I could start building an audience.

It was many nights of no sleep, 18/19 hours of work. I wanted to get the game done a week before the event so I set the early access date for September 13th, and started working on it full-time 14/18 hours a day (90+ hours a week).

About a week before release I had my friend do the trailer & did a large marketing campaign on Reddit. I made memes about the game, I messaged people who commented on the memes, and I just tried to make everyone that I could aware that the game existed.

On release I had a short battle with PTSD. I too vividly remembered the failure of Deep Space, and this game ended up attracting so many people that the servers couldn't handle it. At that point I had already invested $300 into a game that had made no money, it would cost $100/mo out of my savings to upgrade the servers and it looked like the game was doomed to fail, I cried. But I got my act together, I took a leap of faith and invested another $100 into the game, and put up a notice about the servers.

Within a day the game had raised enough money to keep going, and somehow every week people just keep coming back, and I just keep updating the game, and I'm just so happy.

I've been out of work and the game has been able to pay my bills, and now has over [b]200,000 downloads[/b] since release.

But it doesn't stop there. Thanks to this game, I was able to finally have a successful game launch listed on my resume which I showed off when applying for a new job. They were very interested to hear how I had made an entire game on my own (with the exception of many of the starting maps being my friend). I got the job as engineer, and now make a little over $20,000 a year.

Think about that. I had no money for going & no intention of going to college, doing contract work month to month and this game allowed me to finally secure a job in the thing I've been working at my entire life.

This game [b]literally[/b] changed my life. I have the amazing r/dankmemes community & the wonderful people of the internet to thank for it.

So many things had to go right, me deciding to make a game off of a meme, marketing / making memes about it on Reddit, deciding to dig into my own savings in order to keep the servers up, people deciding to get the DLC so that I had enough time to find a job. And people playing every day, talking on the Discord, sharing their thoughts, and making it feel like I actually have people who care about me, and what I've made.

I couldn't ask for more. All I want is for people to enjoy my games, and I've gotten way more than that. I'm truly blessed to have all of you here playing this game and I wouldn't change a thing.

That's why I felt the need to write this. So that when I tell you I'm thankful, you really understand what that means to me, what this game means to me, and what you mean to me.


[h3][b]So really, thank you.[/b][/h3]


I want to continue to make you all proud, and I want to push myself to new limits. So I've decided to start on a new game. I really want to be able to show off my skill & make another game that I can be proud of and that you are all excited to play.

So again, thank you all so much for what you've given me. I promise to do my best to not let you down!

[b]What does this mean for They Can't Stop All Of Us?[/b]
I've been trying my hardest to balance my time but I'm only human. I now do a full-time job, a part-time job, weekly updates for TCSAOU, and am starting work on a new game. I just can't keep up.

I had to start this update expressing how thankful I am, because it'll help give context as to how painful it is for me to say that I just can't keep up the updates. I'm only one man and my time is so fractured I can't keep it together anymore.

This month (December) will be the last TCSAOU updates the game will receive. Every week I've been struggling to come up with new ideas for content, to balance things, new maps, new features, marketing, it's just all so much for one guy to handle. And I don't think it would be a problem if it was my only job but as I stated, I'm making a new game, and have 2 jobs (one full-time & one part-time) so I'm working roughly 80~100 hours a week.

The game will still be available for everyone who wants to play it. So long as people are getting the DLC & the game can pay for its own servers then it'll remain up.

Here are the plans for the future:
[b]12/13/19 (tomorrow):[/b]
New attacker class (DLC Only): theme "Space" with 7 new units & 2 new maps

[b]12/20/19 (Last content update of the game)[/b]
New game mode "Arena" (Defender vs Defender) w/ 3 new maps

There may be updates after that to fix anything broken by the new content but other than that there are no plans for major updates or new content.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]
I really love that you all were there for me, so I want to make you proud moving into the future. The best way to keep up with me & what I'm doing is to join the . I hope to make my next game even half as memorable as this one is!

Sincerely,
Blake Gillman

[h1]Update 9.0[/h1]
Sometimes I just have ideas that could just never work in a normal or balanced game. But with addons, I have the freedom now to create crazy or experimental features that users can choose to opt into or not.

[h1]Addons[/h1]
Addons are a new system which allows players to choose custom parameters to play the game with. In the future this could mean things as simple as giving defenders unlimited ammo to changing the entire game's perspective.

Addon's as a general rule are likely to be buggy, unbalanced, or have other issues - That's why they're addons and not core game features, so that things can be experimented with and users can have fun with those experiments!

If you're using addons, users will get a warning that your server is modified to be different from the default game, and matchmaking won't connect users to your server. This is to prevent new players from having to deal with experimental features while they're still getting used to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35680751/b2ea0981e20d389f840dc8d4bd9a07a98ff55a1a.png[/img]

The first (and only) addon added allows defenders to play in first person mode. This is marked as experimental as there are still several bugs associated with it. Nonetheless it was a ton of fun for me and my friend to test on several maps!

The most unbalanced feature of this addon is seeing enemies coming in-advance in certain scenarios, a fog was placed to prevent this but on maps where the sky is exposed more openly this becomes more of an issue. As for bugs the primary one is that it simply doesn't work with certain outfits which obscure the vision of the first person camera.

notes.title: Medical complications - No update today
notes.content:
Yesterday, at about 7:30 PM I called 911. I thought I was having a stroke because about 5 minutes earlier a nerve in my left temple felt like it pulsated and then my mind went blank & I forgot what I was doing, the left side of my face had begun to feel what I can only describe as like a fuzziness/TV static. These last few weeks I've been having really heavy heartbeats that almost make it feel like my heart is sore from beating. This created what I would call a sense of paranoia regarding my health, and I knew that I was paranoid, so when I had that fuzziness/TV static feeling I ignored it as my mind playing tricks on me, a nocebo if you will. But then suddenly the left side of my face started to go numb, so I picked up the phone and called 911.

The numbness in total lasted about 20 seconds. I called 911 and after about 10 seconds a man answered. I described to him everything that had just happened, as well as my uncertainty since I didn't know whether or not it was my own mind playing tricks on me due to my previous paranoia. He took down my phone number & address, but then I stopped him. I asked him how much an ambulance was and expressed that I didn't know if I could afford one or not because I didn't know if I had health coverage or not. He said he had no idea, and asked if maybe I wanted to call a friend/family to drive me to the hospital, so I said I'd do that.

I called my brother & asked him where he currently was, he was in Canada on a business trip. I told him I needed someone to drive me to the hospital and briefly (in about 4 seconds) explained my symptoms, he said he'd call some nearby family and to wait, so I did.

After about 10 minutes (Or perhaps that's an exaggeration since at this point I was a bit shaken up) he called back saying nobody was there to answer & to call 911. I expressed that I already had but then called him because I didn't know how much an ambulance was or if I could even afford treatment whatsoever (The thought of having large medical debt for the rest of my life was genuinely at that moment nearly as unappealing as the situation because all I could think was how I didn't want to become a slave for the rest of my life to my debt). He told me almost exactly "Dude, just call an ambulance, it's your health" so I said yeah and hung up and re-called 911.

At this point, it felt like I had almost entirely regained feeling in the left side of my face so when a woman answered the call I explained the whole situation, how it initially felt, my current state, and then asked if she thought I was just paranoid and that nothing was wrong. She informed me she couldn't make a medical decision as she wasn't a licensed professional. I asked her if there was any way to ask the EMT's so perhaps I wouldn't have to destroy my savings with an ambulance ride, she said the radio was only for communicating locations & situations. So I decided and said for her to send for an ambulance. She had me on hold for 30seconds ~ 2 minutes (hard to tell in this stressful situation) while she radioed it in, then she told me to wait inside in a comfortable position, to have the front door lights on, and some other general stuff. I told her I'd wait outside instead, the fresh/cold air was nice.

Before the ambulance, a truck arrived with 2 men. One began asking me questions and the other began setting up his equipment for monitoring my vitals on top of my roommate's car (Which at this point it just occurred to me, "Goddamnit I forgot my roommate existed I could've asked him to drive me to the hospital".

I went over the story with them, I also described that drinking mountain dew on some days made the heart problem worse. They asked if I had had any extreme stress. I described how I just had a game release, have been working 80+ hours/week on it, and was getting ready to start on my next project (Forgetting to add that I also have 2 part-time programming contract jobs for other games).

I don't remember if it was the older man or the younger one who said, he'd seen it before and that it was likely a stress-induced problem (stress/anxiety/panic attack). At this point the ambulance was pulling up, I noticed that it had no emergency lights flashing. This indicated to me that my scenario was one of two things:
1) After hearing that I had regained feeling they determined that I was a non-emergency case and didn't need to rush.
2) The 2 people in the truck hadn't radioed back telling them that it was an emergency so they went under the presumption that it wasn't.

Either way, seeing the ambulance's lights off calmed me considerably. I was asked about drug intake if I had had any marijuana, alcohol, off-the-counter drugs, etc. I answered no, said I may or may not have had melatonin (Sleeping pill) the night before but couldn't remember. I asked one of the ambulance driver's recommendation regarding heading to the hospital, and he said that he recommended that I relax, avoid all stimulants such as stress, caffeine, etc. So I decided to go with that option.

During this time while my vitals were being checked & while I was being questioned I had received phone calls from my dad & grandma. My grandma, I had time to answer before the EMT arrived but my dads was during so I didn't. I called back my brother & dad to inform them that I was fine. My brother's girlfriend had arrived on his behalf to make sure that I was okay. notes.content:
[b]Not seeing the update?[/b]
Steam doesn't usually inform the player right away of the update, they tend to wait until you restart your Steam client or until a bit later after the update has come out. So if you want to get the update right away you can do the following:

[h1]Servers[/h1]
Because the game is running on a new backend you won't be able to see servers running on versions previous to 2.1. This means when the update first releases game servers may appear empty.

[h1]Update 2.1[/h1]
This update is entirely dedicated to improving the security of the game. The specifics of the update are a bit complex on the programming side of things, but here's a rundown:

[b]Stopping anti-kick scripts[/b]
Kicking is now more aggressive. This means now that if the game detects that a hacker is attempting to stop the host from kicking them, the server will forcefully close their connection. This is a major improvement to help stop cheaters who the game detects as cheating but who were previously able to block the game from kicking them.

[b]Preventing DLL Injection[/b]
The major improvement with this update is preventing DLL Injection. This form of hack is what the majority of hackers were using to force custom code into the game. This meant changing the backend of how the game was built when uploading updates.

[b]The downsides[/b]
Preventing DLL Injections required changing some fundamentals of the engine which included no longer supporting 32-bit computers. Based off of Steam statistics this is estimated to affect 1% of users.

If you're not sure whether or not your computer is running on 32 or 64-bit on Windows you can check by going to Control Panel > System and Security > System and then check under "System type":

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35680751/024282e8e49e5f43226f6370af886763ca7ecc76.jpg[/img]

This update's backend work also should help improve overall game performance.

notes.title: Hackers & Fake Bans
notes.content:
There are currently hackers in the server who are using tags such as [SUPERADMIN] [ADMIN] or [DEV] to convince people that they are associated with the game, they are not.

Anyone who uses a formal tag such as [Dev] or [Admin] is a hacker. There are no game administrators and we as the developer don't use tags or red names or any color or any indication whatsoever to associate ourselves.

If you've experienced one of these hackers and they "banned" you just note that you have not been banned, Because we only had a month and a half to make the game we made the decision to code the multiplayer client-side as opposed to the more secure server-sided approach. This also means however since we knew the game might be susceptible to hackers we intentionally left out the ability to ban people so that hackers couldn't if they ever got control of the code. They are likely kicking players from the game with a special message that they programmed in to make it look like you've been banned.

That isn't to say that there is no anti-cheat, in fact, a great deal of time was dedicated to stopping people from using basic cheats like spawning materials, speed hacking, etc. However, experienced hackers because of our client-side system are still able to get in since they modify the code directly.

The hard reality of the situation is, unfortunately, because this game was made in such a short period of time we did not design the code in such a way to be completely hacker-proof and it would require us rewriting the game in order to make it that way.

Hackers ruin communities. If you enjoy a game the worse thing you can do is be a hacker because all it does is make people not want to play the game and then you'll have no one to play with.

I sincerely apologize, I've been unable to sleep thinking about this problem and how it's affecting people and myself.

But just remember, if you've been "banned" you haven't actually it's just a hacker writing a custom kick message. And remember that [b]there is no such thing[/b] as a [Dev] or [Admin] or any other kind of special role that exists if you see someone with one they are a hacker. The same goes if their name is a different color.

This is upsetting beyond words. I'm trying my hardest to make a game free for everyone to play and enjoy, and I'll continue to work on it and add new content regardless of hackers. It's upsetting that they would take something I had intended for everyone to enjoy and try to corrupt it.

I will continue to work tirelessly.

Sincerely,
Blake Gillman

I took some time off work in-advance so that I could handle any updates or bugs that came along after release, so if you see a bug don't hesitate to let me know (especially on Discord).

[b]New Features[/b]
[list]
[*] Refresh Button - Originally the game would refresh the servers list automatically, but this created problems due to the player when scrolling getting reset because the servers list would update mid-scroll.
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where if the original host of a game left the room the new host would be unable to start the game

[/list]

[b]Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Improved the fire rate, cooldown, and reload calculations for people on low-end PC. Although if you're getting low fps you're likely going to have a decreased fire rate due to your PC not processing fast enough.

That's it for this update, which really surprises me. I expected a lot worse bugs to appear but I'm really happy that they haven't! The feedback has been absolutely amazing, and I'm really loving all the positivity. The servers have been insanely heavy with players which I'm really happy to see and I hope continues.

notes.title: Welcome to the launch
notes.content:
Today's the day the game finally comes out! So I wanted to go over what the game's development is going to look like from this point forward.

[h1]Weekly Updates[/h1]
Especially with the game just released I want to stay on top of updates. I tend to get anxiety and just want to fix everything as quickly as possible but I've learned from previous games that spacing myself is not only better for my mental health but for the community as well. A predictable schedule helps players play together and not have to worry about updating every day. This means I'll be coming out with an update every week on Friday.

[b]Hotfix Updates[/b]
The exception to this weekly rule would be of course if an update introduces or something is discovered which needs immediate attention such as game-breaking glitches or mechanics.

[b]Patch Updates[/b]
Many of the weekly updates are likely to be patch updates. These are updates which are intended to fix non-essential bugs, add minor features, or general balancing.

[b]Content Updates[/b]
These are the big updates. Any time a new map, class, major feature, etc. is added to the game it'll be a content update. As the game goes on we'll see how often these come but I'm hoping to be constantly adding new content so we'll have to find out.

[h1]Plans for the future[/h1]

[b]Upgrading Servers[/b]
It's yet to be seen whether or not servers will end up being filled, but if current projections are correct then it is likely they will be at some point in the next few days. The game doesn't make any revenue from sales since it's free-to-play but servers and content still cost money to produce. I consider this a passion project so I don't mind that but I can't afford an investment as large as a server. Consider getting the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1147770/They_Cant_Stop_All_Of_Us__Supporters_Edition/]Supporter Edition[/url] which will come with new content in the future as a way of showing your support, with enough people we can upgrade and get everyone playing.

[b]New Content[/b]
One of the major development's of the game, as time goes on, will be brand new content. It's a given that brand new maps, units, and weapons will be introduced. But I also want to add completely new features such as different game modes, and different attacker classes. I still have a fulltime job to do, so the more support the game gets the more of my focus I can give it.

[h1]Be a part of the community[/h1]

[b]Join us on Discord[/b]
The Discord community is a fantastic one where fans of this or my previous games come together to discuss. You can talk about balancing, suggest new features, or just pop in and tell me you're having a fun time :D
[url=https://discord.gg/ArEbAut]https://discord.gg/ArEbAut[/url]

This is all so exciting, I hope to see your room on the list! And thank you so much for the positivity so far, this was just a fun project but the attention it's gotten has been heartwarming.

Sincerely,
Blake Gillman

notes.title: Getting ready for release: New Content!
notes.content:
I've been working fulltime on the game all the way up to release to try and bring new features and content to the game, here are some highlights of content you didn't see in the trailer.

[h1]Brand New Maps[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35680751/106c5ec686548a5e0308d6918c86b24415eb41fc.png[/img]

[u][b]Moon Base 18[/b][/u]
Named after the Apollo 18 mission which established the first outpost on the moon. Troublesome civilians who want to see them moon rocks need to be terminated at all costs! Play as the United States government defending this vital intelligence center, or as civilians whose quest for knowledge is unquenched by the bounds of our atmosphere!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35680751/6b6d3b5ecc27a407267036c98119d9ebd35a0578.png[/img]

[u][b]Tunnels[/b][/u]
The raid enters stage 2! After storming the gate the United States military now flees into the underground tunnels of a key drone facility in charge of defending Area 51. Civilians now rush to destroy their air superiority by any means necessary! Hold your ground and keep those drones in the sky, or be part of the swarm to take them down.

[h1]New Classes[/h1]

[b]Heavy Gunner[/b]
Firepower. We're talking about a fully-loaded M249 machinegun with a 200 round 5.56 belt. It makes you feel powerful, like a proper member of the U.S military.

[b]Sniper[/b]
The sniper doesn't fire often, but they do, it kills. Play as a slow but deadly shooter... and hey, are you wearing a grass ghillie suit in the desert?

[b]Rifleman[/b]
An early version was shown in the trailer, but the rifleman now sports an XM8 fully automatic rifle perfect for concentrated fire!

[b]Support[/b]
Who needs a big gun when your bullets are firing faster than they can move? Equipped with a rapidly firing SMG, having a compact weapon lets you fire fast and reload faster!

[h1]A Shiny New UI[/h1]

[b]Clean Defender UI Update[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35680751/aa813c70b5586a82d512935da52b1a1b24d6795d.jpg[/img]
Players are now sporting more useful information to help them defend the base core! With a new reload & cooldown bar, you're better able to keep track of your firing and adjust strategies on the fly!

[b]Smooth Attacker UI Info[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35680751/3693096c1c7863a3798954e3659c7c1f8d720dd1.jpg[/img]
Knowing what's going on is hard when you've got so many things to keep track of! But the new attacker UI makes this easy with a unit info display box whenever you hover over a spawnable unit. Now you can easily make the decisions necessary to overpower your enemies!

[h1]Changes to the rules[/h1]

[b]Defender Win Timer[/b]
Originally the plan was that defenders would try to survive as long as possible against the attacker. This, however, meant that games could potentially go on for hours! A win timer has been introduced, if the defenders hold out for 20 minutes they win the game!

[b]Attacker Income Timer[/b]
The attacker receiving income every second as shown in the trailer was overkill! The income of the attacker ended up becoming so exponential that the only way the game could last longer than 10 minutes was if the attacker purposefully didn't use their money. Income is still added every time a unit is spawned, but now you only receive that income every 30 seconds!

[b]Attacker Unit Cap[/b]
Unfortunately, as you may have noticed the trailer was a little laggy for the seconds that over 200 units were on the map. Besides being intensive on the computer, it was also intensive on the server as sending that much information constantly was making the units teleport or walk in-place. So the attacker is now capped at 50 units being on the map at once. This also helps to balance as the attacker becomes required to use more and more powerful units as opposed to spamming low-tier ones.

[h1]Join the community! (And the Discord)[/h1]

It has been absolutely insane getting all this done in the short time since the trailer released! I've been doing all-nighter's, drinking Redbull, and it's really started to take a toll on me physically and mentally. But I do it because I love it, and I love to see people having fun playing something I worked so hard on. If you want to discuss the game, report bugs, make suggestions or just let me know that you're having fun playing the game, you can join us on Discord:
[url=https://discord.gg/ArEbAut]https://discord.gg/ArEbAut[/url]

Also consider picking up the Supporter Edition DLC! With the game's insane growth I've added a message to the main menu informing players that you may not get in due to the servers being full! That's insane to think about, but with support I can buy new servers so everyone can play.
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1147770/They_Cant_Stop_All_Of_Us__Supporters_Edition/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/1147770/They_Cant_Stop_All_Of_Us__Supporters_Edition/[/url]

That's all for this update, I hope everyone has a fantastic time playing!

Sincerely,
Blake Gillman
